correctness.rationale: For invertible Euclidean-monotone M, L=||M||2 and gamma>=2, the exact recurrence has C=gamma L M^-1 b, D=-gamma(gamma-1/2)L^2 M^-2 b and E=gamma(gamma-1/2)(gamma-1)L^3 M^-3 b. The three identities MC/L=gamma b, MD/L=-(gamma-1/2)C, ME/L=(1-gamma)D cancel the s^-1, s^-3/2 and s^-2 coefficients of a formal C s^-1/2 +D s^-1 +E s^-3/2 approximation. Residual defect O(s^-5/2). Monotonicity gives ||B_s||<=sqrt((1-gamma/s)^2+1/s)=1-(gamma-1/2)/s+O(s^-2). Discrete convolution yields O(s^-3/2 log s) when gamma=2 and O(s^-3/2) for gamma>2; this is o(s^-1). Neumann expansion of (M+gamma L s^-1/2 I)^-1 then gives universal nonzero lag s(u_k-v_k)->gamma L^2 M^-2 b/2. Independent exact coefficient checks and finite-step simulations on SPD, skew and nonnormal accretive 2x2 matrices corroborated signed coefficients; asymptotics rest on contraction proof, not sampled sequences.

originality.rationale: Cai and Zheng (2026) give the anchored schedule and O(k^-1/2) tangent-residual upper bound; Surina et al. give analogous squared-gradient upper rate; Chen (2026) explains operator-side Tikhonov regularization and an upper rate at gamma=4. Exact two-term vector coefficients and nonzero discrete tracking lag for every invertible monotone M are not given by these upper bounds: an upper rate permits zero leading constant. Best-of-knowledge, with risk from general asymptotic expansions for vanishing regularization.
residual_risks: A general operator asymptotic expansion or Halpern–Tikhonov tracking theorem may imply this linear result.
Constants depend on fixed invertible M and can worsen near singularity.

value.rationale: The theorem gives sharp unavoidable residual bias and the sign/magnitude of the first discrete tracking error for a standard anchored algorithm, including strongly convex quadratics and bilinear skew saddle problems. It distinguishes discretization lag from the target regularization bias, an independently useful quantitative limitation.

limitations: Finite dimensional real M invertible and monotone, nonzero b, gamma>=2; not nonlinear, singular or alternative schedules.
No formal proof-system attestation or floating-point robustness theorem.
